- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-period, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) and price is trending upward; increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.7 → -0.3 → +0.7), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lead time in forecast adjustment.
